citation: Cooper, Heron, & Heward (2020): Prompt Fading & Independence
rationale: An operational definition of 'Independent' responding requires the absence of supplemental stimuli (prompts). Logging a prompt alongside an independent marker is a definitional contradiction.

citation: Cooper, Heron, & Heward (2020): Shaping and Chaining
rationale: Chaining procedures are designed for complex sequences of behaviors (e.g., Daily Living skills). They cannot be applied to discrete academic or communication responses (e.g., identifying a color).

Continuous reinforcement (FR1) is utilized for skill acquisition (teaching new behaviors). Mastered, independent, and fluent skills must be transitioned to intermittent schedules to prevent satiation and mimic natural environments.

rule.right: displaying an absence of maladaptive behavior

citation: Cooper, Heron, & Heward (2020): Discrete Trial Training (DTT)
rationale: DTT requires a controlled environment to minimize distractions and maximize trial velocity. It cannot be conducted in high-mobility or highly distracting natural environments (e.g., water tables, playgrounds).

citation: Cooper, Heron, & Heward (2020): Natural Environment Teaching (NET)
rationale: Incidental teaching and NET rely on capturing naturally occurring motivation in messy/play environments. Highly structured academic materials (flashcards, worksheets) contradict the definition of NET.
